chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who spoke to his wife while he was fasting in the month of Ramadan. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him, and if he emitted semen, there is no penalty upon him, and intimacy is not harmful, and he does not have to make up the day, and it is not appropriate for him to expose himself to Ramadan.'

key_terms.يَتَعَرَّضَ: To expose oneself / to subject oneself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fasting man speaking to or intimating with his wife during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for a man who converses with or engages in intimacy with his wife while fasting, ruling that there is no penalty (kaffarah) even if semen is emitted, and no makeup (qada) is required for that day. This ruling highlights the distinction between acts that break the fast's validity versus those that merely diminish its spiritual perfection, a key nuance in Shia jurisprudence. The Imam adds that while permissible, it is not appropriate (yabghī lahu) to expose oneself to Ramadan, encouraging believers to preserve the sanctity of the month through restraint.
